text: Which type of bifurcation describes oscillatory behavior (a stable limit cycle) emerging from a steady state as a system parameter crosses a critical value?
explanation: A Hopf bifurcation occurs when a complex-conjugate pair of eigenvalues crosses the imaginary axis, causing a fixed point to lose stability and a limit cycle to emerge -- exactly the oscillatory behavior described. A saddle-node bifurcation instead creates or destroys pairs of fixed points (producing bistability), a pitchfork bifurcation involves symmetry breaking into multiple new fixed points, and a transcritical bifurcation exchanges stability between two fixed points that persist across the parameter range -- none of these produce oscillations.
